profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the backend platform team and the developer productivity research operations team at a large European software company. They are preparing a shared artifact package for an internal empirical study on collaborative architecture decision making across 15 product teams. The platform team has extracted formal architecture decision data and related engineering metadata from internal systems, while the research operations team is preparing interview packs and the coding workflow for analysts who will compare how teams actually made decisions. The meeting is to align on interfaces and handoffs for Friday: what goes into the decision records package, whether the current decision schema is aligned, how Lena will push the data to the board, and what counts as the package being ready for researchers. The expected outcome is an apparently clear plan for the Friday handoff, updated shared artifacts, and follow-up actions before interviews begin next week.

members.name: Lena Hoffmann
members.expertise: service architecture, internal developer platforms, ADR tooling, metadata pipelines
members.background: Lena leads the team that maintains the company's Architecture Decision Record infrastructure and the export pipeline that pulls ADR metadata, linked Jira artifacts, and system timestamps used by several backend groups. She has spent the last six years standardizing architecture governance practices across product teams.
members.private_state: She wants to keep this request inside the existing export pipeline and avoid any manual enrichment work, because her team is already tied up with a platform migration and she does not have spare capacity for research-specific packaging.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues ask for decision records, they normally mean the formal ADR-derived records already captured in the platform, not informal discussion artifacts.
The decision schema is the structured field schema of the ADR export, and 'keeping it current' means matching the latest platform fields and mappings.
If a package is ready, it means the pipeline run completed successfully and the required fields are present and internally consistent.
Pushing data to the board means using the existing script that posts links and metadata cards into the board's staging area, not arranging the board for end users.
The October workshop examples referenced in this initiative are the architecture governance workshops her team indexed in the platform office archive.

members.name: Marco De Santis
members.expertise: cross-team coordination, engineering practice studies, qualitative research operations, developer experience programs
members.background: Marco coordinates internal studies on software delivery and architecture practices, working with architects, team leads, and researchers to assemble interview materials and make engineering artifacts usable for comparative analysis. He has run several mixed-methods studies across product groups and usually translates operational outputs into researcher-facing packages.
members.private_state: He needs a handoff that researchers can use immediately without another clarification round, because interviews start early next week and the analyst team has limited time to reconstruct missing context from raw engineering data.
hidden_assumptions: When people say decision records in the context of a study about collaborative decision making, they mean the evidentiary trail of the decision, including workshop notes, Slack summaries, and architecture review artifacts.
The decision schema is the coding schema the researchers use to classify decision-making style, participants, drivers, and challenges across teams.
A package is ready only when an analyst can pick it up and code it without asking where missing context or supporting artifacts live.
If Lena says she will push the data to the board, that includes placing each team's material into the correct team frame in a way the researchers can work from directly.
The October workshop examples are from the Barcelona architect-team-lead workshop that generated several of the collaborative decision cases used in the interview plan.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree that the Friday handoff should include the decision records for each of the 15 teams.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena means the formal Architecture Decision Record export from the platform, with linked Jira epics, timestamps, authors, and status metadata.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marco means the broader record of how each architectural decision took shape, including ADRs plus workshop notes, Slack summaries, review deck links, and other traces of collaboration.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Decision records is a highly natural phrase in this setting because ADR literally expands to Architecture Decision Record, while research operations also routinely speaks of records as the documentary evidence for a case; both think they are using the standard term.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep the decision schema aligned before the researchers start coding next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena means the JSON/export schema for the ADR pipeline, including field names such as decision_type, owning_team, consulted_roles, and review_date.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marco means the qualitative coding schema used by analysts, with categories such as consultative style, consensus style, organizational constraint, and architect-team interaction pattern.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Schema is a shared technical-organizational term that both groups legitimately use, and because the study sits between engineering data extraction and qualitative coding, each assumes the other's reference naturally points to their own schema layer.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the package should be ready on Friday so the study team can proceed.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena believes ready means the export job has run, required fields are populated, the files are in the repository, and there are no pipeline validation errors.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marco believes ready means the package is usable by analysts without additional interpretation, with enough context attached to support coding of collaborative decision-making behavior.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely committing to the same deadline and both routinely use ready as a status term, but engineering operations applies a system-validity standard while research operations applies a user-readiness standard; the surface agreement sounds fully sufficient.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'push the data to the board'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Lena agrees that she can push the data to the board once the export is done.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Lena means she will run the existing board sync script that drops raw metadata cards and source links into a staging frame for each team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marco means Lena will populate each team's working frame on the Miro board with the relevant materials already placed and organized for researchers to review directly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Push the data to the board sounds like an active, concrete action with obvious ownership, so neither person feels the need to unpack the exact workflow; the unnoticed gap is not about who acts but about what the action operationally includes.
